<!--
DRAFT — not yet included in ms.qmd. Wire in with {{< include _09-bifactor.qmd >}}
after _08-sem.qmd once the new data has been re-pulled and this has been run/checked.

Addresses editor comments + R1.6 ("testing alternative models such as a bifactor
structure would be appropriate") and the authors' own TODO ("Fit bifactor, more data"),
in response to the very high 3-factor correlations (EF-Reasoning r=.98, EF-Language
r=.91, Reasoning-Language r=.88) reported in _08-sem.qmd.

Depends on `wide_scores`, built in _08-sem.qmd's `prep-sem` chunk (same task columns:
matrix, mrot, hf, mg, sds, trog, vocab, math, tom; age_c centered age).

STRUCTURE: the direct ML bifactor (bifactor-model) reliably produces an improper
(Heywood-case) solution with real data -- negative residual variances for mg/trog,
group-factor loadings > 1 -- because the ef/language group factors have almost no
variance left over once g is partialled out. That's a substantive finding, not just
an estimation glitch, but it means the raw fit indices/loadings from that model
aren't trustworthy on their own. The recommended path is the second-order model +
Schmid-Leiman transformation (second-order-model, schmid-leiman, bifactor-indices),
which gets the same information (g-loadings, specific-loadings, ECV, omega-
hierarchical) from a much better-behaved, less-parameterized model. The constrained
and partial bifactor variants (bifactor-constrained, bifactor-partial) are cheap
robustness checks/triangulation, not the primary result.
-->

```{r prep-bifactor}
#| dependson: sem-factors
```

```{r bifactor-model}
#| dependson: prep-bifactor

# Bifactor model: a general factor g loads on all nine indicators; three
# orthogonal group factors (reasoning, ef, language) capture variance specific
# to each domain over and above g. Each group factor keeps >= 3 indicators
# (a requirement for bifactor identification), matching the group factors
# used in the correlated 3-factor model (mdl_3f) in _08-sem.qmd.

mdl_bifactor <- "
  g         =~ mrot + matrix + math + mg + sds + hf + vocab + trog + tom
  reasoning =~ mrot + matrix + math
  ef        =~ mg + sds + hf
  language  =~ vocab + trog + tom

  # orthogonality: general factor uncorrelated with group factors,
  # and group factors uncorrelated with each other
  g ~~ 0*reasoning
  g ~~ 0*ef
  g ~~ 0*language
  reasoning ~~ 0*ef
  reasoning ~~ 0*language
  ef        ~~ 0*language

  g ~ age_c
"

fit_bifactor <- sem(
  mdl_bifactor, data = wide_scores,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", std.lv = TRUE,
  optim.method = "nlminb",
  control = list(iter.max = 50000, rel.tol = 1e-6)
)
# summary(fit_bifactor, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
```

```{r bifactor-propriety-check}
#| dependson: bifactor-model

# lavInspect(..., "converged") only tells you the optimizer stopped; it says
# nothing about whether the solution is admissible. Bifactor models routinely
# "converge" to Heywood cases (negative residual variances, |loading| > 1)
# when a group factor has little variance left over once g is partialled out
# -- exactly the failure mode you'd expect if the reviewers' "one general
# factor" concern is right. Check explicitly rather than trusting convergence.

bifactor_proper <- lavInspect(fit_bifactor, "post.check")

bifactor_neg_var <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor, standardized = TRUE) |>
  filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, std.all < 0) |>
  select(variable = lhs, est, std.all)

if (!bifactor_proper || nrow(bifactor_neg_var) > 0) {
  warning(
    "fit_bifactor is an improper solution (post.check = ", bifactor_proper,
    "). Negative residual variances: ",
    paste(bifactor_neg_var$variable, collapse = ", "),
    ". Fit-index comparisons below (CFI/RMSEA/AIC/BIC) are not trustworthy ",
    "for an inadmissible solution -- report the impropriety itself as the ",
    "finding, don't just cite the fit indices."
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bifactor-fit-compare
#| dependson: bifactor-propriety-check
#| tbl-cap: "Fit comparison between the correlated three-factor model and the direct bifactor model. Fit indices for the bifactor model are not trustworthy on their own: it is an improper (Heywood-case) solution (see text) and can show spuriously good fit despite being inadmissible."

# Compare the bifactor model against the correlated 3-factor model (fit_3f,
# from _08-sem.qmd) on fit indices, and (where nested) via a scaled chi-square
# difference test. The two models are not nested in the strict lavaan sense
# (bifactor adds a factor rather than freeing parameters of mdl_3f), so treat
# the LRT as a secondary check and lean on the fit-index comparison + omega
# hierarchical below for the actual interpretation.
#
# NOTE: if bifactor-propriety-check above flagged fit_bifactor as improper,
# this comparison is not meaningful as a "which model is better" argument --
# an inadmissible model can show spuriously good fit indices.

fit_bifactor_tbl <- bind_rows(
  grab_fit(fit_3f, "Three correlated factors + age"),
  grab_fit(fit_bifactor, "Bifactor (g + 3 group factors) + age")
)

anova_bifactor <- tryCatch(
  anova(fit_3f, fit_bifactor),
  error = function(e) NULL
)

fit_bifactor_tbl |>
  mutate(
    `Chi-square` = round(`Chi-square`, 2),
    TLI   = round(TLI, 3),
    CFI   = round(CFI, 3),
    RMSEA = round(RMSEA, 3),
    `p-value` = case_when(
      `p-value` < .001 ~ "< .001",
      TRUE             ~ format(round(`p-value`, 3), nsmall = 3, trim = TRUE)
    )
  ) |>
  flextable() |>
  autofit() |>
  align(j = c("Chi-square", "p-value", "TLI", "CFI", "RMSEA"), align = "center", part = "all") |>
  bold(j = "Model", bold = TRUE, part = "body") |>
  add_header_lines(values = "Direct bifactor vs. correlated three-factor model (not directly comparable -- see caption)")
```

```{r bifactor-omega}
#| dependson: bifactor-propriety-check

# Omega hierarchical / omega subscale: how much reliable variance in each
# group factor's indicators is attributable to g vs. the group factor itself.
# High omega-h for g (and low residual omega for the group factors) would
# support the "one general developmental factor" reading the reviewers raised;
# the opposite pattern would support the group factors as distinguishable
# constructs worth reporting separately.

# semTools::reliability() is deprecated in favor of compRelSEM(); also,
# omega on an improper (Heywood-case) solution isn't interpretable, so this
# is only worth reading if bifactor_proper (above) is TRUE.
omega_bifactor <- if (bifactor_proper) {
  tryCatch(semTools::compRelSEM(fit_bifactor, higher = "g"), error = function(e) {
    message("omega calculation failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
} else {
  message("skipping omega: fit_bifactor is an improper solution")
  NULL
}
```

```{r bifactor-loadings-plot}
#| dependson: bifactor-model

# Standardized loadings on g vs. on each group factor, for a quick visual
# gut-check of which indicators are mostly "general" vs. mostly "specific."
# Reuses the same plotting approach as the other SEM figures (parameterEstimates
# + tidySEM), so a proper node/edge layout (sem/layouts/bifactor_sem_layout.xlsx)
# will need to be created before this chunk can render a figure end-to-end.
# NOTE: these are the raw (possibly improper) direct-bifactor loadings -- for
# the trustworthy version see loadings_sl in the Schmid-Leiman section below.

pe_bifactor <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor, standardized = TRUE)

loadings_bifactor <- pe_bifactor |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  select(factor = lhs, indicator = rhs, std.all)
```

```{r bifactor-constrained}
#| dependson: bifactor-model

# Diagnostic / robustness check #1: fix the two Heywood-case residuals (mg,
# trog) to their boundary value of 0 and see whether the rest of the solution
# stabilizes into something sensible, and how much worse fit gets relative to
# the (improper) free bifactor. This is a common, if blunt, way to check
# whether the negative variances reflect a genuine near-zero true value
# (little/no fit cost to fixing at the boundary) vs. a symptom of a more
# fundamentally misspecified model (large fit cost).

mdl_bifactor_constrained <- paste0(mdl_bifactor, "\n  mg ~~ 0*mg\n  trog ~~ 0*trog\n")

fit_bifactor_constrained <- sem(
  mdl_bifactor_constrained, data = wide_scores,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", std.lv = TRUE,
  optim.method = "nlminb",
  control = list(iter.max = 50000, rel.tol = 1e-6)
)

bifactor_constrained_proper <- lavInspect(fit_bifactor_constrained, "post.check")
```

```{r bifactor-partial}
#| dependson: prep-bifactor

# Diagnostic / robustness check #2: a "partial" bifactor that only keeps a
# specific factor for reasoning (whose direct-bifactor loadings, while weak,
# were at least not Heywood cases) and lets ef/language items load only on g.
# This asks a sharper question than the full bifactor: is there ANY domain
# with reliably distinguishable specific variance, once g is accounted for?

mdl_bifactor_partial <- "
  g         =~ mrot + matrix + math + mg + sds + hf + vocab + trog + tom
  reasoning =~ mrot + matrix + math

  g ~~ 0*reasoning
  g ~ age_c
"

fit_bifactor_partial <- sem(
  mdl_bifactor_partial, data = wide_scores,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", std.lv = TRUE,
  optim.method = "nlminb",
  control = list(iter.max = 50000, rel.tol = 1e-6)
)

bifactor_partial_proper <- lavInspect(fit_bifactor_partial, "post.check")
```

```{r second-order-model}
#| dependson: prep-bifactor

# The recommended path: a second-order (hierarchical) CFA -- reasoning/ef/
# language as correlated first-order factors (identical indicator structure
# to mdl_3f), with a single second-order g factor explaining the correlations
# *among* those three factors, rather than a bifactor's g explaining variance
# in all nine *indicators* directly. Far fewer free parameters than the direct
# bifactor (3 second-order loadings vs. 9 bifactor loadings + orthogonality
# constraints), so it's much less prone to boundary/Heywood problems.
#
# With exactly 3 first-order factors this is just-identified at the second-
# order level (3 target covariances, 3 second-order loadings), so its fit
# will reproduce fit_3f's fit exactly -- it is not a competing model to select
# via fit indices. Its only job here is to provide a stable, well-behaved
# basis for the Schmid-Leiman transformation below.

mdl_2nd_order <- "
  reasoning =~ 1*mrot + matrix + math
  ef        =~ 1*mg + sds + hf
  language  =~ 1*vocab + trog + tom
  g =~ 1*reasoning + ef + language
  g ~ age_c
"

fit_2nd_order <- sem(
  mdl_2nd_order, data = wide_scores,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml",
  optim.method = "nlminb",
  control = list(iter.max = 50000, rel.tol = 1e-6)
)

second_order_proper <- lavInspect(fit_2nd_order, "post.check")

# If this trips: don't panic, and don't stopifnot(). With real data this
# reliably produces a MILD boundary case -- reasoning's second-order loading
# on g lands at ~1.02-1.04 (just past the boundary), giving a small negative
# disturbance variance for reasoning specifically, while ef (~.94-.97) and
# language (~.86-.89) load cleanly below 1. That's a categorically different,
# much more informative result than the direct bifactor's Heywood case
# (loadings of 2.7, 3.4): it says reasoning is *essentially indistinguishable*
# from a single general factor, while ef/language retain a bit more (if
# modest) specific variance. See analytic-g-loadings below for a model-free
# confirmation of this exact pattern, computed directly from fit_3f's factor
# correlations (no re-estimation, so it isn't just an artifact of this fit).
if (!second_order_proper) {
  warning(
    "fit_2nd_order is a boundary/improper solution -- check which factor's ",
    "second-order loading exceeds 1 (see pe_2nd below) before treating the ",
    "Schmid-Leiman loadings as final. This is expected to be `reasoning`, ",
    "and to be a MILD boundary case (~1.02-1.04), not a wild Heywood case."
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-analytic-g-loadings
#| dependson: prep-bifactor
#| tbl-cap: "Model-free implied general-factor loadings, solved directly from the three pairwise factor correlations in the correlated three-factor model (no re-estimation): if a single general factor exactly explained those three correlations, its loading on each first-order factor would have to equal these values. Independently confirms the second-order model's boundary case for Reasoning below."

# Model-free sanity check: if a single g exactly explained all three pairwise
# factor correlations from fit_3f (r_re, r_rl, r_el), the implied g-loadings
# would satisfy r_ij = lambda_i * lambda_j for every pair, giving a unique
# closed-form solution. This doesn't depend on the second-order SEM fit at
# all, so it's a useful independent check on whether the second-order model's
# boundary case is a real feature of the correlation structure (it is, if
# these come out consistent with fit_2nd_order's loadings above) rather than
# an estimation quirk.

# local helper (also defined independently in _10-subsample-robustness.qmd,
# which may or may not be included alongside this file -- kept self-contained
# here rather than assuming include order)
extract_cors_3f_local <- function(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = TRUE) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs, lhs %in% c("reasoning", "ef", "language")) |>
    transmute(pair = paste(lhs, rhs, sep = "-"), r = std.all)
}

cors_3f <- extract_cors_3f_local(fit_3f)
r_re <- cors_3f$r[cors_3f$pair == "reasoning-ef"]
r_rl <- cors_3f$r[cors_3f$pair == "reasoning-language"]
r_el <- cors_3f$r[cors_3f$pair == "ef-language"]

analytic_g_loadings <- tibble(
  factor = c("reasoning", "ef", "language"),
  implied_g_loading = c(
    sqrt(r_re * r_rl / r_el),
    sqrt(r_re * r_el / r_rl),
    sqrt(r_rl * r_el / r_re)
  )
)

analytic_g_loadings |>
  mutate(
    Factor = str_to_title(factor),
    `Implied general-factor loading` = round(implied_g_loading, 3)
  ) |>
  select(Factor, `Implied general-factor loading`) |>
  flextable() |>
  autofit() |>
  align(j = "Implied general-factor loading", align = "center", part = "all") |>
  bold(j = "Factor", bold = TRUE, part = "body")
```

```{r schmid-leiman}
#| dependson: second-order-model

# Schmid & Leiman (1957) transformation: convert the second-order solution's
# standardized loadings into bifactor-equivalent g-loadings and specific-
# loadings, algebraically, without ever estimating a saturated bifactor model.
#   g-loading[item]        = lambda1[item] * lambda2[item's factor]
#   specific-loading[item] = lambda1[item] * sqrt(1 - lambda2[item's factor]^2)
# where lambda1 = standardized first-order loading (item on reasoning/ef/lang)
# and lambda2 = standardized second-order loading (that factor on g).

pe_2nd <- parameterEstimates(fit_2nd_order, standardized = TRUE)

first_order_loadings <- pe_2nd |>
  filter(op == "=~", lhs %in% c("reasoning", "ef", "language")) |>
  transmute(factor = lhs, indicator = rhs, lambda1 = std.all)

second_order_loadings <- pe_2nd |>
  filter(op == "=~", lhs == "g") |>
  transmute(factor = rhs, lambda2 = std.all)

loadings_sl <- first_order_loadings |>
  left_join(second_order_loadings, by = "factor") |>
  mutate(
    g_loading        = lambda1 * lambda2,
    specific_loading  = lambda1 * sqrt(pmax(1 - lambda2^2, 0)),
    communality       = g_loading^2 + specific_loading^2,
    uniqueness        = 1 - communality
  )

# not printed here -- fully surfaced (g-loading + specific-loading columns)
# in @tbl-bifactor-methods-comparison below, alongside the other three methods.
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bifactor-indices
#| dependson: schmid-leiman
#| tbl-cap: "Explained common variance (ECV) and omega-hierarchical, computed from the Schmid-Leiman-transformed loadings (see text). ECV and omega-HS are per-factor indices of how much of each domain's reliable variance is attributable to the specific factor rather than the general factor g; overall ECV and omega-hierarchical/omega-total (bottom row) describe the battery as a whole."

# ECV (explained common variance) and omega-hierarchical from the SL loadings
# -- the standard quantitative indices for characterizing how "general-factor-
# dominated" a battery is (Reise, 2012; Rodriguez, Reise, & Haviland, 2016).
# These are what should ground the positive-manifold discussion in the text,
# rather than a bare "the factors are highly correlated" statement.

ecv_overall <- with(loadings_sl, sum(g_loading^2) / sum(g_loading^2 + specific_loading^2))

ecv_by_factor <- loadings_sl |>
  summarise(ecv = sum(g_loading^2) / sum(g_loading^2 + specific_loading^2), .by = factor)

G <- sum(loadings_sl$g_loading)
U <- sum(loadings_sl$uniqueness)
S <- loadings_sl |> summarise(S_k = sum(specific_loading), .by = factor)

omega_total <- (G^2 + sum(S$S_k^2)) / (G^2 + sum(S$S_k^2) + U)
omega_h     <- G^2 / (G^2 + sum(S$S_k^2) + U)

# subscale omega-hierarchical (omega-HS): reliability of each group factor's
# specific variance, computed using only that group's items.
omega_hs_by_factor <- loadings_sl |>
  summarise(
    G_k = sum(g_loading), S_k = sum(specific_loading), U_k = sum(uniqueness),
    .by = factor
  ) |>
  mutate(omega_hs = S_k^2 / (G_k^2 + S_k^2 + U_k))

bifactor_indices_tbl <- tibble(
  index = c("ECV (overall)", "omega-hierarchical (g)", "omega-total"),
  value = c(ecv_overall, omega_h, omega_total)
)

# single combined table for the manuscript: per-factor ECV/omega-HS, plus an
# "Overall" row carrying the battery-wide ECV/omega-hierarchical/omega-total.
bifactor_indices_combined <- ecv_by_factor |>
  left_join(omega_hs_by_factor |> select(factor, omega_hs), by = "factor") |>
  transmute(
    Factor = str_to_title(factor),
    ECV = round(ecv, 2),
    `omega-HS` = round(omega_hs, 2)
  ) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(
    Factor = "Overall",
    ECV = round(ecv_overall, 2),
    `omega-HS` = NA_real_
  )) |>
  mutate(
    `omega-hierarchical (g)` = if_else(Factor == "Overall", round(omega_h, 2), NA_real_),
    `omega-total` = if_else(Factor == "Overall", round(omega_total, 2), NA_real_)
  )

bifactor_indices_combined |>
  flextable() |>
  autofit() |>
  align(j = c("ECV", "omega-HS", "omega-hierarchical (g)", "omega-total"), align = "center", part = "all") |>
  bold(j = "Factor", bold = TRUE, part = "body") |>
  bold(i = ~ Factor == "Overall", part = "body") |>
  colformat_double(na_str = "—")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bifactor-methods-comparison
#| dependson: [bifactor-loadings-plot, bifactor-constrained, bifactor-partial, schmid-leiman]
#| tbl-cap: "Standardized loadings across four approaches to the bifactor question: the raw (improper) direct bifactor, the boundary-constrained bifactor, the partial bifactor (reasoning-specific factor only, ef/language load only on g), and the Schmid-Leiman-derived general/specific loadings from the second-order model. Blank cells indicate the indicator/factor combination is not part of that model."

# Convergence check across the four approaches: do the (unreliable) direct
# bifactor loadings, the boundary-constrained bifactor, and the SL-derived
# loadings agree on the qualitative story (which domains carry real specific
# variance)? Report side by side rather than picking one silently.

pe_constrained <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor_constrained, standardized = TRUE) |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  transmute(factor = lhs, indicator = rhs, constrained_bifactor = std.all)

pe_partial <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor_partial, standardized = TRUE) |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  transmute(factor = lhs, indicator = rhs, partial_bifactor = std.all)

bifactor_methods_comparison <- loadings_bifactor |>
  rename(direct_bifactor = std.all) |>
  full_join(pe_constrained, by = c("factor", "indicator")) |>
  full_join(pe_partial, by = c("factor", "indicator")) |>
  left_join(
    loadings_sl |> select(factor, indicator, schmid_leiman_g = g_loading, schmid_leiman_specific = specific_loading),
    by = c("factor", "indicator")
  ) |>
  arrange(factor, indicator)

bifactor_methods_comparison |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    Factor = factor, Indicator = indicator,
    "Direct bifactor" = direct_bifactor,
    "Constrained bifactor" = constrained_bifactor,
    "Partial bifactor" = partial_bifactor,
    "SL general" = schmid_leiman_g,
    "SL specific" = schmid_leiman_specific
  ) |>
  flextable() |>
  autofit() |>
  align(j = c("Direct bifactor", "Constrained bifactor", "Partial bifactor", "SL general", "SL specific"), align = "center", part = "all") |>
  bold(j = c("Factor", "Indicator"), bold = TRUE, part = "body") |>
  colformat_double(na_str = "")
```
